best_for: Students, planners and GIS hobbyists who need historical imagery or GIS file import on the desktop, and who can live with an app Google stops offering in mid-2027.

points.title: Downloads end June 25, 2027
points.text: Google says Google Earth Pro on desktop will no longer be available for download from June 25, 2027. Plan for the web or mobile versions if you need it beyond that.

points.title: What Pro adds
points.text: Compared with the web version, the desktop app offers historical imagery and GIS import and export, aimed at users with advanced needs. There is no charge listed for it.

points.title: Modest hardware
points.text: Google lists 2 GB of RAM, 2 GB of free disk and DirectX 9 or OpenGL 1.4 graphics as the minimum, with 4 GB of RAM and a dual-core 2 GHz chip recommended. You need an internet connection to load imagery.

points.title: Old systems still listed
points.text: The help page lists Windows 7 and Mac OS 10.8 on a 64-bit Intel chip as minimums. Street View needs version 7.3.3 or newer.

points.title: Linux: prefer Google's packages
points.text: Google offers 64-bit .deb and .rpm packages and tests on Ubuntu and Fedora. The Flatpak here is x64 only, unverified, not affiliated with Google, and still at 7.3.6 while Windows and macOS have 7.3.7.1327.

points.title: Install details
points.text: Windows installers come in 32-bit and 64-bit and install for all users. The Mac download is one universal disk image. The Windows listing keeps 9 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
